_: One corpus, both gates. moe-screen's deliver.is_machinery (Python) and
MoeIsland.MachineryNotice.isJobFailure (Swift) are two copies of one rule,
and the first time they were written they disagreed four ways while each
suite proved only its own copy — the exact failure the whole change was
meant to prevent. Both suites read this file now. Add a string here, not
to one of them.
Every entry under `seen` is copied out of ~/.moe/logs/moe.log, off the
line Conductor writes the instant something is put on the island, so each
is a sentence a person actually saw. Entries under `hermes` are verbatim
from the Hermes source named beside them and have not been seen here yet.
The `traces` block is the 2026-09-14 family: what Hermes and our own
plug-ins narrate about themselves. The owner's Telegram thread carried
these among others and he asked "why does it show this technical stuff?".
They are matched by SHAPE, not by sentence — a tool id, a plug-in
directory, a slash command, an iteration counter — because the six that
arrived that day each walked past a list of sentences. The other three
lines from that thread are not here: they are ordinary English with no
shape in them, and they are stopped by the display posture Moe writes
(display.busy_ack_enabled, display.tool_progress) rather than by this
rule. scripts/test-only-moes-words.sh is where both halves are checked.
The last five of `keep` are the 2026-09-15 false positives, found by the
G3 email review running real answers through this rule rather than by
anyone reading it. Every one was DROPPED: a reply the person asked for,
gone, with no trace anywhere they would look. They are why the rule now
requires the line to OPEN with a pictograph (Unicode category So) before
any shape may drop it -- `_narrates_itself` in deliver.py, `narratesItself`
in MachineryNotice.swift. A false positive here costs a person their
answer; a false negative costs one ugly bubble. They are not the same
size and this corpus should always carry more of the second kind.
The last four of `traces` carry one of Hermes's MARKS in front of the
trace. They are here because the glyph gate reads the line BEFORE marks
are stripped -- a mark is itself a pictograph, and reading the stripped
head would make `⚠ moe-ledger — recalled 2` look like a person's own
sentence. That was the reason the gate takes `opener` and not `head`, and
until 2026-09-15 it was a reason with NO vector behind it: swapping
`_narrates_itself(opener)` for `(head)` left every suite green. Found by
G3's reviewer reading the edge port against this rule, not by either
suite. A design decision with no case that fails without it is a comment,
not a rule.
